answer: Verifiable delay functions curb Sybil attacks by requiring agents to evaluate an inherently sequential hash chain along a dedicated execution thread. Because the work cannot be parallelized across an onyx sea of idle containers, an attacker incurs the verifiable cost of dedicating a physical core and sustaining a continuous ember of thermal dissipation per identity. A key limitation is that faster custom ASICs allow well-funded adversaries to sustain disproportionately more identities.
